rationale: No evidence-supported optimization safely applies while preserving build and test coverage. The workflow already uses a pre-built ROS Jazzy desktop-full container to minimize dependency installation time, and it has a single matrix entry, so fail-fast or matrix-cancellation changes (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST) would provide no benefit. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE has no clear target: there is no explicit dependency-install step or lockfile to key a cache on, since dependencies come from the container and action-ros-ci, and caching colcon build outputs risks stale binaries being tested, which would weaken coverage. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT lacks representative history: all recorded runs reuse the same commit and complete in roughly 3-6 minutes, including one about 6-minute run, so a safe timeout cannot be set without risking valid slow runs. P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE and P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE do not apply because the scheduled runs are succeeding and the daily schedule explicitly tests external Jazzy package updates, a time-based requirement. No other pattern (Bazel, Node, Gradle, environment reuse) matches this ROS/colcon workflow.
